prompt: The movements of people from the villages to the cities for work has caused a lots of problems in both places. What are the serious problems associated with this? What measures can be taken to solve these problems?
essay:
The migration from rural areas to cities has gained momentum over the last half of a century. It poses numerous issues for both villages and towns. This essay will shed some light on the main problems of such a phenomenon and provide several plausible solutions to resolve the same.

Firstly, mass migration can exert severe pressure on finite land resources and skyrocket real estate prices. For instance, Hong Kong faced such a problem at the beginning of the twenty-first century, and today, an average apartment costs approximately twenty years of family income. To resolve such a predicament, governments throughout the world should develop a fast internet connection and pass new regulation measures to make their economies more decentralized.

Moreover, when youngsters leave their families in small towns to excel in big cities, it creates additional risks for senior citizens who lose necessary support and puts additional pressure on healthcare systems. For example, according to a study conducted at the University of North Carolina, seniors without children and grandkids support spend twenty-three per cent more on health-laden issues. It is recommended that a group of small cities with reasonable accommodation prices in one particular area instead of developing infinite megalopolises be developed to make it possible to move the whole family during the immigration process and cut some costs.

Although the domestic migration phenomenon provides new opportunities for the young generations, it has its own drawbacks. It is predicted that technological development may help to make neglected rural areas great again.
